en: The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest eagles in the world.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his ancestral home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines is the highest court and holds the judicial branch of the national government.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago using advanced indigenous engineering and irrigation systems.
Fe del Mundo was the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator for rural areas.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño through a traditional two-steps-forward, one-step-back dance.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system where each character represents a syllable rather than a single letter.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is demonstrated when community members work together to physically relocate a neighbor's nipa hut.
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, citizens who are at least eighteen years old have the right and duty to vote.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan and the Oblation statue at the University of the Philippines.
Andres Bonifacio founded the Katipunan, a secret society that initiated the armed revolution against Spanish colonial rule in 1896.
Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.
